idiom_name: sealed Command ADT on Behavior[Command] + ActorSystem.terminate/Coordinated Shutdown + ask for status
implementation_notes: In a Pekko (or Akka) system the control bus is the actor protocol and the supervision hierarchy: control commands are ordinary typed messages - the typed API literally parameterises the actor with its command type - lifecycle control is explicit (a child can stop itself or be stopped by its parent, stopping the guardian actor terminates the ActorSystem, and ActorSystem.terminate runs Coordinated Shutdown, which stops actors and services in a defined order), and status is collected with the ask pattern or a Snapshot message carrying an ActorRef for the reply. Parent-stop recursively stops children, so a component tree can be quieted with one message to its root, which is the closest thing to a control bus the framework offers.
code_sketch:
sealed trait Command
case object Pause extends Command
case object Resume extends Command
case class Snapshot(replyTo: ActorRef[Status]) extends Command

def apply(): Behavior[Command] = Behaviors.setup { ctx =>
  var draining = false
  Behaviors.receiveMessage {
    case Snapshot(replyTo) => replyTo ! snapshot(draining); Behaviors.same
    case Pause  => draining = true;  Behaviors.same
    case Resume => draining = false; Behaviors.same
  }
}

system.terminate()   // coordinated shutdown: actors and services stop in a defined order
pitfalls: ActorContext is not thread-safe and must not be used from Future/ask callbacks (the Pekko docs call this out): a control handler that does so corrupts actor state - commands must stay in the message-processing thread.
Terminate is asynchronous and runs Coordinated Shutdown phases, so code that assumes the system is gone right after terminate() races its own shutdown hooks.

Classic-API PoisonPill/Kill are mailbox messages with different cleanup semantics (Kill throws inside the actor and can skip cleanup); the typed API's explicit Stop message is the safer control contract.

variants.name: JMX MBeans from Scala (platform MBean server)
variants.idiom_name: StandardMBean over a Scala control trait registered in the platform MBeanServer
variants.implementation_notes: The JVM's platform MBean server is available from Scala unchanged: implement a control trait, wrap it in StandardMBean (or use Spring's @ManagedResource) and register it under an ObjectName, so status is exposed as attributes and commands as operations to jconsole, JMX connectors and monitoring agents. This is the interoperability choice - JMX consoles and agents speak to Scala and Java components alike - while the Pekko variant is better when lifecycle is hierarchical and commands are naturally messages.
pitfalls: Scala `val`/`var` members become attributes with the same visibility: a `var` is a remotely writable state field, so all mutation must go through operation methods that validate.
Registration failures (duplicate ObjectName, missing MBean interface) are easy to swallow in a try/catch during startup, leaving the component running with no control surface at all.
JMX operations run on the connector thread, so a long-running command blocks the console and can deadlock with the actor's mailbox if it waits on a reply synchronously.
